table_title: List the 15 crops globally most produced by 2024 tonnage per FAOSTAT, grouped by Continent of Top Producer to show the geographic distribution of major global crop production. Universe filter: FAOSTAT QCL (Crops and Livestock Products) domain, Area=World, Element=Production, Year=2024, individual crop items only, excluding aggregate rows and livestock/animal products. For each top-15 crop, give the Continent of Top Producer (closed 5-value categorical — Africa / Asia / Europe / North America / South America; Oceania not in 2024 top-15 producers), Top Producing Country (sovereign-country name per FAOSTAT with largest 2024 production share), Global Production (million tonnes) at 6-decimal precision per FAOSTAT, and FAO Crop Group (FAOSTAT classification — closed 6-value: Sugar crops / Cereals / Oil crops / Roots and tubers / Vegetables / Fruits). Note: Russian Federation is classified as Europe per FAOSTAT's transcontinental-state convention (Russia's primary production is in European Russia for sugar beet + barley).
db_analog: WITH top_15 AS (SELECT crop_item_label, continent_of_top_producer, top_producing_country, global_production_million_tonnes_2024, fao_crop_group FROM faostat_qcl_world_production_2024 WHERE element = 'Production' AND area = 'World' AND year = 2024 AND item_type = 'individual_crop' AND NOT is_aggregate AND NOT is_livestock ORDER BY global_production_million_tonnes_2024 DESC LIMIT 15) SELECT * FROM top_15 ORDER BY continent_of_top_producer ASC, global_production_million_tonnes_2024 DESC
temporal_note: FAOSTAT Crops and Livestock Products (QCL) domain, accessed via cycle-1 audit's master-derived dump on 2026-05-18. Universe is the closed top-15 crops globally most produced by 2024 tonnage per FAOSTAT QCL with explicit filters: Area=World, Element=Production, Year=2024, individual crop items only, excluding aggregate rows and livestock/animal products. Year-lock 2024 — FAOSTAT publishes annual updates; when 2025 data becomes available, instance can be re-staged (temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this). source_count = 1 registered (FAOSTAT QCL domain — universe + value role for 3 of 5 cells per cycle-2 audit's source-extraction language refinement: Crop, Global Production, Top Producing Country are FAOSTAT-extractive; Continent of Top Producer and FAO Crop Group are deterministic normalization/classification cells derived from FAOSTAT's country + crop item taxonomy). Per-row cells: Crop name verbatim from FAOSTAT item labels (e.g., 'Maize (corn)', 'Cassava, fresh', 'Onions and shallots, dry (excluding dehydrated)' — parentheticals preserved per audit); Global Production at 6-decimal precision in million tonnes (e.g., Sugar cane 1939.782021); Top Producing Country in FAOSTAT-canonical full official forms ('United States of America', 'Russian Federation' — NOT abbreviations); Continent of Top Producer per deterministic 5-value mapping (Brazil → South America; United States → North America; India / China / Indonesia → Asia; Nigeria → Africa; **Russian Federation → Europe** per FAOSTAT's transcontinental-state convention); FAO Crop Group per FAOSTAT classification taxonomy (Sugar crops / Cereals / Oil crops / Roots and tubers / Vegetables / Fruits — closed 6-value vocabulary). Cycle-2 audit's required edits applied at cycle-0: (1) gt_construction = web_search_faostat (NOT manual_wikipedia per existing local validator pattern accepting web_search_* for non-Wikipedia sources); (2) sort = Continent of Top Producer ASC + Global Production DESC within continent (foregrounds geographic distribution per cycle-2 audit's category-alignment requirement); (3) source-extraction language refined to distinguish FAOSTAT-extractive cells (Crop / Production / Top Producer) vs deterministic normalization cells (Continent / Crop Group); (4) source_url uses FAOSTAT UI landing page; direct QCL bulk download URL is referenced in source_coverage_notes as more reproducible alternative.
_extraction_notes: Geographic instance — closed canonical top-15 FAOSTAT 2024 crops universe ordered by Continent of Top Producer ASC alphabetic (Africa → Asia → Europe → North America → South America) then Global Production (million tonnes) DESC within continent. Per-continent distribution: Africa 1 (Cassava); Asia 9 (Rice, Wheat, Oil palm fruit, Potatoes, Tomatoes, Bananas, Onions, Watermelons, Apples); Europe 2 (Sugar beet, Barley); North America 1 (Maize); South America 2 (Sugar cane, Soya beans); Oceania 0. Asia-dominant (9 of 15) reflects China + India + Indonesia agricultural concentration. Single PK Crop (FAOSTAT item labels unique within the 15-entry universe). **Brings `geographic` from gap 1 (4 of 5) to gap 0 (5 of 5) — SATURATES `geographic` as the 14th fully-cleared category** (joining factual_lookup, top_k, multi_hop, qualitative, multi_attribute_projection, set_operation, set_filter, causal, implicit_join, scaled_enumeration, hierarchical_decomposition, comparative, temporal). Food family extends from 1 to 2 instances — **crisis-light family chip** (Food was previously at 1 instance only via `vitamins_top5_food_sources` Food/Nutrition; this brings Food to 2 with NEW Food/Agriculture subdomain). Only Health remains as crisis-light family at 1 instance. NEW `agricultural-commodities/crops` fine-class within a NEW `agricultural-commodities` entity bucket per cycle-2 audit's 'agricultural-commodities/crops would be more semantically precise' note. Audit also accepted `taxonomic-entities/crops` as an existing-bucket alternative. Source plan: 1 registered source (FAOSTAT QCL domain UI URL — universe role: top-15 ranking by 2024 production; value role for 3 of 5 cells: Crop name, Global Production, Top Producing Country; the other 2 cells — Continent of Top Producer, FAO Crop Group — are deterministic normalization/classification per cycle-2 audit's source-extraction language refinement). NO per-crop validation sources documented — FAOSTAT alone is authoritative for all 5 cells via its country-taxonomy + crop-classification taxonomy. claim_type = source_defined per cycle-2 audit confirmation, with explicit filter: 'FAOSTAT QCL, Area=World, Element=Production, Year=2024, individual crop items only, excluding aggregate rows and livestock/animal products'. Cycle arc: 2 rounds of pre-staging design review (cycle-1 'Revise' with 4 BLOCKING — source change to FAOSTAT / universe corrections / 5th column choice / category fit; cycle-2 'Approve With Required Edits' — gt_construction / sort-order / source-extraction language / source URL precision). Cycle-2 audit's master-derived 15-row dump used verbatim at cycle-0 staging — all 75 cell values (15 rows × 5 cols) committed from FAOSTAT verbatim per audit's dump. Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable include Sugar cane Brazil top producer (#1 by tonnage globally), Maize United States (#2), Rice China/India top producers, Wheat China, Soybean Brazil; mid-difficulty include Oil palm fruit Indonesia, Cassava Nigeria (Africa's top food crop), Sugar beet Russia (European crop); harder calibration include Barley vs Sweet potato boundary (Barley in top-15 at rank 11; Sweet potato displaced — common knowledge says Sweet potato is in top-15 staples but 2024 FAOSTAT data shows otherwise), Onions+shallots verbose FAOSTAT label, exact 2024 production values at 6-decimal precision, Russia=Europe transcontinental-state convention. Geographic category-fit (cycle-2 audit confirmed via title foregrounding + sort order): per-Continent partitioning emphasizes geographic distribution; Asia 9 dominant signals agricultural concentration in the most-populous continent; mirror precedent `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (uneven per-continent distribution with master Asia-heavy 5/16). Saturates the geographic category leaving only `aggregation` (4/5) at gap-1 — one more aggregation instance would saturate the FINAL gap-1 category and bring benchmark to 15/15 SATURATED state.
